 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 In fairness, there were times in that second half where things did get a little more exciting.
 More shots and more goalmouth action than the first, for sure.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 4 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:31 GMT 18:31 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 A battle, a scrap, a chore. Call it what you like, it happened and now it's over. A point apiece a fair result.
 35 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:27 GMT 18:27 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Now we're on the same page, Paul.
 Storm Boelo was the winner at the Stadium of Light. The wind made it incredibly difficult for either side to play anything resembling attractive football.
 74 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:25 GMT 18:25 GMT 
 FT: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 It was a tough game and a tough watch at times. We saw two sides that are trying to be resilient. 
 66 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 FULL-TIME published at 18:23 GMT 18:23 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 That's it. It ends goalless so Sunderland remain bottom of the table. A fifth draw in eight league games leaves Leeds in seventh.
 159 58 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 18:23 GMT 18:23 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' to have your say 
 This Sunderland game has been the best cure for my hangover. Fell asleep at the end of the first half (awful game) and have just woken up feeling much better! Did I miss anything?
 Nick 
 370 125 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:22 GMT 18:22 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Image source, Getty Images The ball is flashing from left, to right across the Sunderland goal area. 
 125 38 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 CLOSE! published at 18:22 GMT 18:22 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 How has that not gone in for Leeds?!
 A deep cross is nodded back across goal, Sean Longstaff swings a boot at it but his shot is cleared a yard off the line.
 Leeds keep possession, though, another cross comes in and this time it's hammered across goal by Noah Okafor.
 It hits a defender, could go anywhere but, thankfully for Sunderland, it's just wide of the post. Corner.
 98 65 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:21 GMT 18:21 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 No nonsense stuff from Omar Alderete, thumping the ball out for a throw in.
 Leeds with the ball, then, with a little over two minutes left of stoppage time.
 190 57 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:20 GMT 18:20 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Sunderland come forward now and after James Trafford fails to deal with a long ball, the home side have a corner.
 Ah. Well, that wasn't very good, I'm afraid. Chemsdine Talbi's flies high over everyone and out for a goal kick.
 243 91 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:19 GMT 18:19 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 The wind is definitely with Sunderland right now. 
 100 184 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 INJURY TIME published at 18:19 GMT 18:19 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Teasing delivery with everyone crowded around the goalkeeper, the ball breaks loose and rolls towards the edge of the box... but there are no Leeds players there to capitalise.
 There are going to be SIX added minutes.
 122 75 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:18 GMT 18:18 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 As I type that, Leeds break forward and Sean Longstaff's low shot from 20 yards has to be pushed wide by Robin Roefs.
 Leeds corner. Sunderland just about deal with it but Leeds win another...
 370 71 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:17 GMT 18:17 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Image source, Getty Images Less than a minute left of the 90. We await to see how much added time there will be but, at this stage, a goal would come as something of a shock.
 119 37 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 SUBSTITUTION published at 18:15 GMT 18:15 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 One more change for Leeds.
 Ao Tanaka is off and former Newcastle midfielder Sean Longstaff is booed onto the pitch by the home fans.
 188 77 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:14 GMT 18:14 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 James Trafford bundled into Tarik Muharemovic as he claimed that high ball and both of them then go down.
 After a bit of treatment, they're both up, though. Three minutes left of the 90.
 159 35 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:13 GMT 18:13 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Sunderland are pushing for a winner as we enter the last five minutes of the 90 but James Trafford comes out to make a very impressive claim as a cross is swung to the back post.
 252 67 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:12 GMT 18:12 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 The wind has just picked up hasn't it. You can see all of the rubbish blowing around this stadium. 
 133 69 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:12 GMT 18:12 GMT 
 Sunderland 0-0 Leeds 
 All valid points, as were Harry's others. However, there is no denying that Sunderland are bottom of the table despite that.
 Anyway, a Sunderland long throw from the right gets caught up in the wind - I'd worked so hard not to mention it as much this half - and is blown straight out for a goal kick.
 81 40 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 18:09 GMT 18:09 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' to have your say 
 Arsenal fan, but Harry [@ 18:02] is right. Sunderland are going to be fine. They are better than at least six of the eight teams above them. Good to see the same media nonsense from last year, acting as if the first gainful of games decides the league, is still ever-present.
 Kris 
 Harry has a point. They've faced Arsenal, City, and Brighton already, and that's the top three.
 Z 
 In Harry's defence we all know Man City are actually bottom of the table, but we'll leave that can of worms there for today...
 Aidan
